about: Trainer: torque balance (Unit 5). Explore: a meter stick on a fulcrum (masses, the fulcrum's position, an angled pull) with live clockwise and counterclockwise torque bars and the beam tipping with alpha = net torque / I; and a rotational inertia race. Test yourself: problems from ApPhysMath.torqueBalance.generate; the validator recomputes every key for 300 seeds per context.
intro: A meter stick balanced on a fulcrum, with masses you hang and a pull you aim. The bars show the clockwise and counterclockwise torques about the fulcrum; when they are equal the stick stays level, and when they are not it tips with the angular acceleration α = τnet / I. The second scene races two wheels with the same mass spread differently.
howItWorksTitle: Torque, equilibrium and α = τ / I
howItWorks:
• Torque about a pivot: τ = r F sin θ, where r is the distance from the pivot to where the force acts and θ the angle between r and the force. Equivalently, force × lever arm, the perpendicular distance from the pivot to the force's line of action. A force through the pivot has no torque.
  • Rotation is described as clockwise or counterclockwise about the axis. Here counterclockwise counts as positive.
  • A uniform stick's own weight acts at its center (its center of mass).
  • Equilibrium needs both Στ = 0 (about any point) and ΣF = 0. Taking torques about an unknown force's point removes it from the equation.
  • Newton's second law for rotation: α = τnet / I. Rotational inertia I = Σ m r² for point masses; for the stick about its center, (1/12) M L² (given, never memorized), plus M d² when the pivot is a distance d from the center.
  • The beam stops tipping when an end reaches the table. The masses hang on short strings and move with the beam. g = 9.8 m/s².

Numbers count within 2% (positions on the stick within 4 mm).
